title: WO INT8 compatibility, failover policies, and synthetic eval bench for GPTQ/AWQ
creator: Asha Patel
description: Deliver an integration and regression test suite that validates weight-only INT8 (GPTQ and AWQ) quantization profiles across representative model families, with explicit failover policies to FP16/FP32 variants when accuracy or numeric instability is detected. This ticket scopes the synthetic evaluation bench, CI canary plumbing, and the playbook for automated rollback/fallback behavior if drift thresholds are breached.
acceptance_criteria: Synthetic evaluation harness runs end-to-end in CI and produces a summary JSON with per-model token-diff, BERTScore, and answer EM statistics
Canary pipeline can deploy an INT8 WO profile to a shadow fleet and automatically compare outputs vs FP16 baseline within configured tolerances
Failover policy implemented: automatic route to FP16 model if (<accuracy_threshold> OR <numerical-failure-rate> > threshold) for 10 minutes
Regression alerts surface to runtime-telemetry dashboard with clear links to failed prompt sets and PR that introduced change
Documentation (Confluence) with playbook steps for manual triage, rollback, and customer communication is published and reviewed
notes: 2026-02-26 — Kickoff: scoped core bench and list of representative models (Llama variants, Mistral-style, and smaller instruction-tuned checkpoints). Chosen seed sets for deterministic runs.

2026-03-02 — Decision: use deterministic tokenization seeds + fixed RNG for GPTQ retraining runs to reduce night-to-night drift. Trade-off: slight loss in exploratory coverage but huge gain in reproducibility.

2026-03-04 — Implemented initial synthetic prompt set (2.4k prompts across domains: math, coding, summarization, tokenization-edge cases). Stored in GCS: gs://redwood-quant/bench/wo-int8/seed-20260304.json

2026-03-06 — Perf trade-off discovered: AWQ profiles produce lower memory but higher variance on long-sequence code generation. Flagged in test harness; added per-sequence-length bucketing for thresholds.
2026-03-08 — PR submitted: github.com/redwood-inference/quant/pull/4821 (adds bench runner, baseline comparator, BERTScore wiring). Requesting eng review from @maria-ng and @kyle-tan.

2026-03-10 — Canary plan approved in runbook review. Added automatic fallback TTL=5m and a 3-step escalation: automated rollback -> paging to oncall -> create postmortem if rollback fails to restore fidelity.

2026-03-12 — Running cross-model sweep with shadow canary. Early telemetry: for long-tailed token distributions AWQ median EM drop=2.1 points vs GPTQ 1.2 points. Need to tune AWQ quant params for kernels on A100 L4-like hardware.
Follow-ups: schedule kernel-selection experiment with infra (ENG-937000) and add focused numeric stability tests for attention-softmax tails.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: AWQ's dynamic range on older kernels causes sporadic NaNs for >2048 seq -> Mitigation: add pre-deploy numeric gate that runs a 50-sample softmax-stability probe and blocks profile if NaNs observed.

Risk: Synthetic bench may not cover customer-specific prompt distributions -> Mitigation: add customer prompt ingestion whitelist for enterprise Dedicated accounts and a labelled drift detector in Optimize to trigger private evals.
Risk: Canary churn due to upstream model changes -> Mitigation: pin model versions in canary lanes and provide compatibility matrix in PR templates.
next_steps: Finish PR review and merge bench wiring (blocking: infra@oncall for ephemeral GPU slots)
Run full model-family sweep (24h) with both GPTQ and AWQ profiles and collect per-seq-length buckets
Tune AWQ quant params for long sequences and re-run sensitivity tests
Add CI gate that fails merges if nightly regression > configured thresholds for any model in the golden set
Publish Confluence playbook and schedule a 30-minute runbook review with SRE and Customer Success
review_feedback: @maria-ng: Please surface the exact numeric thresholds in the acceptance criteria. Suggest using BERTScore >= 0.92 for summarization tier and EM delta <= 1.5 for short answers.
@simon-cho: Need a documented rollback SMS/pager path in runbook for Enterprise customers; added to playbook.
@kyle-tan: Recommend adding token-level KL divergence metric for distributional drift in addition to BERTScore/EM.
